Thanks Marissa — that recap is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- When we say PII we mean any free-text prompts that could contain customer identifiers, and any metadata you store that could be linked back to our users (user_id, email).
- We need evidence that a deletion request will remove data from: (a) live indices/datastores, (b) KV caches used during inference, (c) routine logs (access logs, audit logs), and (d) backups/snapshots within a reasonable SLA.
- For backups, our security policy requires that within 90 days of a deletion request there is no recoverable copy of the deleted PII. We understand some systems have longer immutable retention windows; please call out any constraints.

Looping in Acme Legal (legal@acmecorp.com) to align on wording we'll expect in SOW/contract.

Also — Wednesday 2/18 works on our side. Would like Dev and your security lead on the call.

Hi Sarah — thanks, and great questions. Below is a technical note summarizing how Redwood handles deletion/RTBF and where constraints exist. High level first, then specifics.

High level:
- Live data (customer prompts, responses, metadata) stored in customer-scoped stores are deleted on request. For hosted customers we offer both immediate logical deletes and background purges depending on the store.
- KV cache used for inference is ephemeral (per-instance) and does not persist across long-term storage — clearing it prevents future usage, and caches are cleared on deletion requests.
- Audit and access logs: production access logs are separated into (a) operational logs (short-term, used for debugging), (b) audit logs (security/forensics). We can configure retention windows; by default operational logs are 30 days, audit logs 365 days.
- Backups/snapshots: we take periodic snapshots for disaster recovery. Snapshots are immutable for the duration of the snapshot retention policy. Our standard hosted snapshot retention is 90 days; during that time a deleted record may exist in a snapshot. We provide a documented purge workflow that marks data as deleted and ensures it is not restored to live services, and we can commit to removing data from future snapshots after 90 days. If you require <90-day recovery window, we can discuss a shorter retention SLA as part of Dedicated/Private deployments or via a contractual exception.

Specifics / timeline options we can offer:
- Immediate logical delete from live stores: within 24 hours of request.
- Cache purge: immediate (within minutes) for any running instances.
- Operational logs purge: configurable; can be reduced to 7/30/90 days per contract.
- Audit logs: typically 365 days; we can provide redaction options for PII fields on request, with evidence logs of redaction actions.
- Backup snapshot purge: snapshots are scheduled; we can implement an expedited purge workflow to exclude the deleted identifiers from next snapshot rotation, but note immutable snapshots already taken cannot be modified; therefore full elimination from backups typically completes once retention window expires (standard 90 days).

Additional notes:
- For Private (customer-managed) deployments we can provide tooling and runbooks so your ops team can run an expedited purge (including removing data from backups) if you require that control.
- For Dedicated customers we can commit to custom backup retention policies and provide audit evidence for deletion to satisfy SOC2/ISO-type audits.
- We keep a deletion audit trail (who/when/request id) and can provide hashes/records showing deletion action without exposing deleted content.

Attachments included: RTBF-process-v1.docx (Marissa attached a draft checklist) and I also attached a short FAQ I use with legal teams (I'll paste below).

FAQ (short):
Q: Can you guarantee no copy exists in backups immediately?
A: Not for immutable snapshots already taken; guarantee applies post-retention window unless contractual exception granted.

Q: What about logs that are used for billing/analytics?
A: Billing data can be retained separately; we can scope PII redaction for billing records per contract.

Q: What evidence do you provide?
A: Deletion request id, timestamp, affected object ids, confirmation of logical delete, and later a statement confirming backup retention window elapsed and no recovery is possible.
